title: Derelict Hours: a co-op space salvage horror game I'm building in Unity with Claude Code, Codex and Tripo AI. Here's the full workflow, and I'm looking for playtesters.
author: GunnforgeStudio
selftext:
Hey gang. I'm the solo dev behind \*\*Gunnforge Studios\*\*, and for the last few weeks I've been building \*\*Derelict Hours\*\*, a first-person co-op horror game for PC, with AI tools doing a lot of the heavy lifting. This sub seemed like the right place to share how it's actually put together, warts and all.

https://reddit.com/link/1y0w7aw/video/oaqtq8o7mp2i1/player

\*\*The game\*\*

You and up to three friends crew a cheap, rented salvage dropship on the Crysal Frontier. You dock with dead freighters, board in the dark, strip what you can carry, and get back to the ship before the wreck's failing reactor runs out the clock, or before the thing living deep in the ship finds you.

\- \*\*Every freighter is different.\*\* Hand-built rooms, procedurally laid out across three decks from a seed, with stairs, narrow catwalks over open cargo bays, and loops so chases have somewhere to go.

\- \*\*Proximity voice is the game.\*\* You hear your crew from where they stand, muffled through walls, and the creatures hear you too. Calling out for help can bring the Hark.

\- \*\*The Hark can't be killed.\*\* It lives in the deepest rooms (where the best loot is) and its patrol widens as it gets stirred up by noise and time.

\- \*\*Greed vs. getting out.\*\* A 12-minute run clock, no sirens, the ship tells you through flickering lights and hull jolts. Whoever's inside the airlock when it shuts made it; anyone else is left behind with what they carried.

\- \*\*Between runs\*\* you're in a hub station: sell salvage at the broker, keep your rented ship running (or finance it and hope you don't miss a payment), feed its Crysal core, kit out your suit, and build up your own hangar base.

https://i.redd.it/ft5fch9kmp2i1.png



\*\*How it's built: the workflow\*\*

The short version: I'm the designer, director and playtester. The AI tools are the team. Nothing ships without me deciding it and checking it.

\*1. Design first, in plain documents.\*

Everything starts in three files in the repo: a \*\*GDD\*\* (every decision dated, with who made it), a \*\*ROADMAP\*\* of small milestones, and a \*\*WORKFLOW\*\* doc for how we work. The AI reads these before touching anything. Open questions get settled one at a time when the roadmap needs them, not up front.

\*2. Claude Code builds, then explains.\*

Claude Code (Anthropic) does most of the implementation: C# systems, netcode, editor work. The rules it works under:

\- \*\*One task per branch\*\* off \`main\`, small enough to finish and check in one sitting.

\- \*\*Engine first.\*\* If a Unity developer would build it in the editor (scenes, prefabs, Animator controllers, audio mixers, URP volumes, NavMesh), it's built in the editor through a \*\*Unity MCP relay\*\* that lets Claude drive the editor directly, not generated from scripts. Code is for behaviour.

\- \*\*Ask before guessing.\*\* When there's more than one reasonable route, it stops and asks me with a recommendation.

\- \*\*Every multiplayer feature is tested with a host plus one client\*\* (Unity's Multiplayer Play Mode) before it's called done.

\- Each handoff ends with an explanation of the key Unity/C# ideas, so I understand my own codebase, and one concrete thing for me to check in the editor.

https://i.redd.it/ht77w1hwmp2i1.png

\*3. Art: Tripo AI, Codex concept art, Blender.\*

\- Final 3D models come from \*\*Tripo AI\*\*, either text-to-3D (Claude writes the prompt and drives it into a running Blender through an MCP server) or image-to-3D from \*\*concept art I generate with Codex\*\*.

\- Every prompt states real-world size in metres and that the design has to be original to this game.

\- Everything goes through \*\*Blender\*\* before Unity: a template file with a 1.8 m reference human, pivot and naming rules, and an export script that lands FBX in Unity at the right scale every time.

\- Where Tripo can't give exact-fit modular pieces (wall kits, salvage props), Claude builds them as scripted Blender models with baked procedural materials instead.

\- The hub's crowd uses the \*\*MakeHuman\*\* base body (CC0) through the MPFB add-on, with a randomised character builder for 300 NPCs. Animations are \*\*Mixamo\*\*.

\*4. Audio.\* A licensed sound library (Sonniss) plus synthesis, cut and mixed in Unity's audio mixer.

\*5. The launcher.\* \*\*Codex\*\* is building the \*\*Gunnforge Launcher\*\* as its own project: accounts, friends, invites and game updates. The game talks to it so you can invite friends straight into a session.

\*6. The website and backend.\* Claude Code also built \*\*gunnforgestudios.com\*\* (plain JavaScript + Vite on Netlify) and its \*\*Supabase\*\* backend: one account system shared by the site and the launcher, a forum, game ownership, Stripe checkout, and the playtest application below. Same rules as the game: Claude proposes the database design, I approve it, and it tests the security rules (who can read and write what) before anything goes live.

\*\*Tech stack\*\*

Unity 6 (URP), Netcode for GameObjects (host-and-join), Unity Relay for online play, Vivox for proximity voice, ProBuilder for greyboxing, AI Navigation for creature pathing.

\*\*What I've learned so far\*\*

\- AI is fast at systems and slow at taste. The design docs and "ask before choosing" rule matter more than any prompt.

\- Writing decisions down with dates saves you. When something breaks three weeks later, the reason for the design is right there.

\- Multiplayer needs real two-machine tests. Plenty of bugs only show up host + client, never in single player.

\- AI 3D generation is great for props and hero pieces, and bad at anything that has to snap to a grid.

\*\*Want to play?\*\*

We're getting ready for the first proper playtests: Windows PC, small groups, voice chat strongly encouraged. It's a game for 1–4 players, so \*\*crews get priority.\*\*

\- \*\*Apply to playtest:\*\* [https://gunnforgestudios.com/#/playtest](https://gunnforgestudios.com/#/playtest). It takes about three minutes. Apply with your crew by listing your friends' Gunnforge player names (they need a free account, but they don't have to fill in the form). Applying solo? Tick "match me" and we'll put you with other testers.

\- \*\*Create a free account:\*\* [https://gunnforgestudios.com/#/account](https://gunnforgestudios.com/#/account)

\- \*\*More about the game:\*\* [https://gunnforgestudios.com/#/games/derelict-hours](https://gunnforgestudios.com/#/games/derelict-hours)

We're bringing testers in a group at a time. Testing is free for approved testers: you'll get an email, and the game shows up in your Gunnforge Launcher library.

Happy to answer anything about the workflow, the tools, or the game in the comments.
